title: Histidine-rich Modification of a Scorpion-derived Peptide Improves Bioavailability and Inhibitory Activity against HSV-1.
extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism layer; automated nucleic-acid locator note was rejected as not paper-specific mechanism evidence.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Eval418 acts at early extracellular HSV-1 infection steps, with direct viral inactivation and inhibition of viral attachment/entry supported by time-of-addition and plaque reduction assays.
mechanism_claims.mechanism_strength: phenotypic_direct_antiviral_step_assay; molecular viral target not identified
mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper supports infection-step phenotype, not a resolved molecular binding target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Poor cellular uptake limits Eval418 post-entry activity; FITC localization and time-of-addition results support this as a distribution/bioavailability limitation.

source_locator.locator: xml:fig=4:panel=f; xml:sec=results Eval418 blocks initial steps

mechanism_claims.limitations: Cellular uptake is linked to post-entry antiviral activity, but intracellular molecular target is not demonstrated.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Histidine-rich Eval418 derivatives, especially Eval418-FH5, improve cellular uptake/distribution and post-entry HSV-1 suppression while retaining extracellular viral inactivation and attachment activity.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Eval418-FH2, Eval418-FH3, Eval418-FH4, Eval418-FH5; strongest support for Eval418-FH5
mechanism_claims.limitations: Histidine-rich modification is supported as a design/uptake strategy; exact molecular antiviral target remains unresolved.
